title: After Losing Her Limbs, Our Cooking Columnist Returns to the Kitchen

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费者产品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《周日每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Iwande Komalafe is a cooking columnist here at The Times.
sentences.zh: 伊万德·科马拉费是本报的一位烹饪专栏作家。

sentences.en: She's worked for many years in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 她在餐厅工作多年。

sentences.en: She's known for translating complicated restaurant dishes into recipes for the home cook.
sentences.zh: 她以将复杂的餐厅菜肴转化为家庭烹饪食谱而闻名。

sentences.en: Her cookbook, My Everyday Lagos, was nominated for a James Beard Award.
sentences.zh: 她的食谱书《我的日常拉各斯》曾获詹姆斯·比尔德奖提名。

sentences.en: But almost three years ago, Komalafe's life took a dramatic turn when she nearly died in the midst of a sickle cell crisis.
sentences.zh: 但大约三年前，科马拉费的生活发生了剧变，当时她在镰状细胞危象中险些丧命。

sentences.en: When she woke up from a weeks-long coma, she learned that her body would be profoundly altered by multiple amputations.
sentences.zh: 当她从长达数周的昏迷中醒来时，她得知自己的身体因多次截肢而发生了深刻的改变。

sentences.en: Now, Iwande is back to work, creating recipes and writing again.
sentences.zh: 现在，伊万德重返工作岗位，再次开始创作食谱和写作。

sentences.en: Today, Iwande spoke with me from her kitchen in Brooklyn about what it has been like to return to her life after this crisis
sentences.zh: 今天，伊万德在布鲁克林的家中与我交谈，讲述了她在经历这场危机后重回生活是什么样的感受，

sentences.en: and how cooking and food played an essential role in her recovery.
sentences.zh: 以及烹饪和食物在她的康复过程中发挥了怎样的重要作用。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, August 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月2日，星期日。

sentences.en: Iwande, welcome to The Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 伊万德，欢迎来到《周日每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Before we talk about everything that you've been through,
sentences.zh: 在我们谈论你所经历的一切之前，

sentences.en: I wonder if you can explain what sickle cell disease is and how it affects the body for our listeners who are not familiar with this disease.
sentences.zh: 我想请你为不太了解这种疾病的听众解释一下什么是镰状细胞病，以及它如何影响身体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So sickle cell is an inherited blood disorder.
sentences.zh: 镰状细胞病是一种遗传性血液疾病。

sentences.en: I was born with it.
sentences.zh: 我天生就有。

sentences.en: I've always known I've had it.
sentences.zh: 我一直都知道自己患有这种病。

sentences.en: And so the shape of normal cells are spherical.
sentences.zh: 正常细胞的形状是球形的。

sentences.en: And in that way, normal cells are able to pass through your arteries, your veins, your capillaries.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，正常细胞能够通过你的动脉、静脉和毛细血管。

sentences.en: But sickle cells are literally sickle-shaped.
sentences.zh: 但镰状细胞字面意思就是镰刀状的。

sentences.en: And it's almost like there's like half of them missing.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像缺失了一半一样。

sentences.en: And in that way, when they try to pass through your artery, your veins, your capillaries, they sometimes get clogged.
sentences.zh: 所以当它们试图通过你的动脉、静脉和毛细血管时，有时会造成堵塞。

sentences.en: And that could result in a very painful crisis of like the joints.
sentences.zh: 这可能导致关节等部位出现非常痛苦的危象。

sentences.en: And it almost feels like a pain that you can't quite touch.
sentences.zh: 那种疼痛感几乎让你无法触及。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: It's like an internal pain.
sentences.zh: 那是一种内在的疼痛。

sentences.en: And I've grown up with this disease.
sentences.zh: 我从小就带着这种病长大。

sentences.en: I've always known I've had it.
sentences.zh: 我一直都知道自己有这种病。

sentences.en: And I would also credit my family and my mom for teaching me how to take care of myself, both using natural medicine and using Western medicine.
sentences.zh: 我也要感谢我的家人和母亲，她们教会了我如何照顾自己，既使用自然疗法，也使用西医。

sentences.en: How did all of that affect how you worked in the restaurant industry?
sentences.zh: 这一切是如何影响你在餐饮业的工作的？

sentences.en: Like what kind of adjustments did you have to make in order to have the jobs that you did?
sentences.zh: 为了胜任你的工作，你必须做出什么样的调整？

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting because I never thought of sickle cell as something that would hold me back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为我从未认为镰状细胞病会阻碍我。

sentences.en: I understood that if I was able to take care of myself, literally drink a gallon of water every day,
sentences.zh: 我明白，如果我能照顾好自己，比如每天喝一加仑水，

sentences.en: do things like that, pace myself through the work, get enough sleep and get enough rest,
sentences.zh: 做这些事情，在工作中调整节奏，保证充足的睡眠和休息，

sentences.en: I can manage my disease.
sentences.zh: 我就能控制我的病情。

sentences.en: And so if I worked a long shift, I knew that I needed like three to four days to recover from that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我上了一个长班，我就知道我需要三到四天的时间来恢复。

sentences.en: And so it was a lot about, it was a lot of like just understanding my body to an extent where I knew that if I did go ahead and push myself to that limit,
sentences.zh: 所以这很大程度上是关于了解我的身体，以至于我知道如果我真的把自己推向极限，

sentences.en: you're not going to see me for like 10 days because I'll be sick.
sentences.zh: 你就得有十天见不到我了，因为我会病倒。

sentences.en: That sounds really challenging.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很具挑战性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it took a lot of coming to terms with the fact that I have it, even though it's easy for me to talk about now, but it wasn't always easy for me to say or highlight that,
sentences.zh: 所以这需要花很多时间去接受我患有这种病的事实，尽管现在谈论起来很容易，但对我来说，说出或强调这一点并不总是那么容易，

sentences.en: oh, like I have this disease.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有这种病。

sentences.en: And I think I was also in a position where I looked normal, like compared to everybody else, I looked like I was normal, whatever normal was.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我当时处于一种看起来很正常的状态，和别人相比，我看起来很正常，无论正常是什么定义。

sentences.en: When you say normal, I'm curious what your life looked like when you were a recipe developer.
sentences.zh: 当你提到正常时，我很好奇当你作为食谱开发者时，你的生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: I wonder if maybe you could just walk us through a typical day for you before this medical crisis happened.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能为我们描述一下在这场医疗危机发生前，你典型的一天是怎样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel like an average day for me would start by writing the recipes and then sourcing the ingredients.
sentences.zh: 好的，我觉得我的一天通常是从写食谱开始，然后去采购食材。

sentences.en: So like going around to different grocery stores, go to the markets and like feel and touch and see the vegetables that I was getting and then start preparing them.
sentences.zh: 比如去不同的杂货店、市场，去感受、触摸和观察我买到的蔬菜，然后开始准备它们。

sentences.en: However, the recipes specified.
sentences.zh: 按照食谱的要求去做。

sentences.en: Sounds like you're running around a lot.
sentences.zh: 听起来你一直在奔波。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And usually like it would be depending on what I'm working on, I would be stove side or like in the kitchen between like one to I would say I sometimes went on till like 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，取决于我在做什么，我会待在炉边或者厨房里，从一点一直忙到晚上8点左右。

sentences.en: But I'm always thinking about food.
sentences.zh: 但我总是想着食物。

sentences.en: So it's it's never really like there's like a turn on and turn off switch.
sentences.zh: 所以从来没有所谓的开关。

sentences.en: It's like I dream about food.
sentences.zh: 我甚至会梦见食物。

sentences.en: I dream about creating recipes, you know, and in my excitement, sometimes I wake up and like jot that down or take notes if I remember my dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我梦见创作食谱，你知道，在兴奋之余，有时我会醒来把它们记下来，如果我记得梦的内容的话。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So you dreamt about food.
sentences.zh: 所以你梦见食物。

sentences.en: I can imagine that means that you have been quite passionate about it for some time.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象这意味着你对它已经充满热情很久了。

sentences.en: Where do you think that interest came from?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种兴趣是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: I think I mean, I would say that my mom definitely like was the catalyst for that.
sentences.zh: 我想，我会说我母亲绝对是其中的催化剂。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: So I grew up in Lagos, Nigeria, and my mom was a food scientist and she worked for Cadbury's Chocolates,
sentences.zh: 我在尼日利亚的拉各斯长大，我母亲是一位食品科学家，她在吉百利巧克力公司工作，

sentences.en: but she also would bring things home to sort of like test out on us as kids.
sentences.zh: 但她也会带一些东西回家，让我们这些孩子试吃。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Because I remember this about my childhood is that we always had like a five pound bag of all sorts of candy.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得童年时，我们总有一大袋各种各样的糖果。

sentences.en: And it was usually stuff that she was working on.
sentences.zh: 通常都是她正在研发的东西。

sentences.en: She was particularly working on how to develop a chocolate that's like shelf stable in the Nigerian heat that doesn't completely collapse and dissolve.
sentences.zh: 她特别致力于研发一种在尼日利亚的高温下能保持稳定、不会完全塌陷和融化的巧克力。

sentences.en: And like she would try out the different tests on us.
sentences.zh: 她会让我们尝试不同的测试。

sentences.en: I saw it my entire childhood.
sentences.zh: 我整个童年都看在眼里。

sentences.en: And so moving here, I first signed up to be a biochemist like like her and did not have that did not happen.
sentences.zh: 所以搬到这里后，我最初报名想成为像她一样的生物化学家，但那并没有发生。

sentences.en: But I had actually encountered a pamphlet from the CIA while I was living with.
sentences.zh: 但我其实在我住的地方偶然发现了一份美国烹饪学院（CIA）的小册子。

sentences.en: Yeah, wait, you're the Culinary Institute of America.
sentences.zh: 等等，你是说美国烹饪学院。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not not that CIA.
sentences.zh: 不是那个中央情报局（CIA）。

sentences.en: Like the Culinary Institute was about to take a weird turn.
sentences.zh: 我还以为烹饪学院的故事要往奇怪的方向发展了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd come across a pamphlet and I was like intrigued.
sentences.zh: 是的，我偶然看到了一本小册子，当时很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, wow, you could go to school to be a chef.
sentences.zh: 我想，哦，哇，原来还可以去学校学做厨师。

sentences.en: And so I sort of like put that in my back pocket and I went to college and I felt like that was for my parents.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它记在心里，但我还是去读了大学，我觉得那是为了我的父母。

sentences.en: And going to culinary arts school was felt like the first decision that I made for myself.
sentences.zh: 而进入烹饪艺术学校，感觉是我为自己做的第一个决定。

sentences.en: Eventually transitioned from being in restaurant kitchens to being in your own kitchen, of course, writing about food, writing about not just cooking, but adapting recipes.
sentences.zh: 最终，你从餐厅厨房转到了自己的厨房，当然，开始写关于食物的文章，不仅是关于烹饪，还有关于改编食谱。

sentences.en: It's one of the things that you have been known for.
sentences.zh: 这是你出名的原因之一。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little bit about what your life was like in November 2023, right before you got very seriously ill?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们你在2023年11月，也就是你病重之前的生活是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was great.
sentences.zh: 是的，那段日子很棒。

sentences.en: I had just finished my first book and I was in the middle of my book tour.
sentences.zh: 我刚完成了我的第一本书，正处于新书巡回宣传期间。

sentences.en: I had done a few events.
sentences.zh: 我参加了几场活动。

sentences.en: I had gone to Lagos.
sentences.zh: 我去过拉各斯。

sentences.en: I had gone to all the New York events.
sentences.zh: 我去过纽约所有的活动。

sentences.en: And my husband, my two kids and I went to Paris for Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 我和丈夫以及两个孩子去巴黎过了感恩节。

sentences.en: And we came back.
sentences.zh: 然后我们回来了。

sentences.en: We were all sick.
sentences.zh: 我们都病了。

sentences.en: We all had like contracted something like either in the airport or like just by flying.
sentences.zh: 我们都在机场或者飞行途中感染了什么东西。

sentences.en: Like with the flu or a cold or something?
sentences.zh: 比如流感或感冒之类的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, we didn't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不知道。

sentences.en: We didn't know what it was, but we knew that we were all sick.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是什么，但我们知道我们都病了。

sentences.en: Eventually that weekend, I decided that I was in too much pain to try to treat it at home.
sentences.zh: 那个周末，我最终决定疼痛太剧烈了，无法在家治疗。

sentences.en: You mean sickle cell pain?
sentences.zh: 你是说镰状细胞带来的疼痛？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I went to the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了急诊室。

sentences.en: We found out I had influenza A, which is actually very deadly for people who are immunocompromised.
sentences.zh: 我们发现我得了甲型流感，这对免疫功能低下的人来说其实非常致命。

sentences.en: And so I got dropped off at the ER by my husband.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫把我送到急诊室。

sentences.en: He took the kids back home.
sentences.zh: 他把孩子们带回了家。

sentences.en: I only remember through several text messages that I sent both to my husband as like an update of the status.
sentences.zh: 我只记得通过几条发给丈夫的短信更新了我的状况。

sentences.en: And what I kept saying was that I'm in a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 我一直在说我非常疼。

sentences.en: I'm still in a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 我还是很疼。

sentences.en: And I can tell from that that my pain wasn't being managed.
sentences.zh: 从这一点我可以看出，我的疼痛没有得到控制。

sentences.en: But you don't remember this period.
sentences.zh: 但你不记得这段时间了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't remember this part.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不记得这段时间了。

sentences.en: But I know what to ask for when I go to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 但我知道去医院时该要求什么。

sentences.en: I'm like, I need oxygen.
sentences.zh: 我会说，我需要氧气。

sentences.en: I need fluid, like IV fluids.
sentences.zh: 我需要输液，静脉输液。

sentences.en: And I might need a blood transfusion.
sentences.zh: 我可能需要输血。

sentences.en: And I need pain medication.
sentences.zh: 我需要止痛药。

sentences.en: Those are the four things that I asked for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我要求的四件事。

sentences.en: And this time, it felt like the things that I asked for were not given to me.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，感觉我要求的东西并没有给我。

sentences.en: And there was a whole series of errors that happened and weren't corrected.
sentences.zh: 发生了一连串的错误，而且没有得到纠正。

sentences.en: And that's why things escalated in the way that it did.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么情况会升级到那种地步。

sentences.en: So what happened after that?
sentences.zh: 那之后发生了什么？

sentences.en: I woke up in a different hospital.
sentences.zh: 我在另一家医院醒来。

sentences.en: Completely different hospitals.
sentences.zh: 完全不同的医院。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And everybody's faces looked worried.
sentences.zh: 每个人的脸上都写满了担忧。

sentences.en: I was told that I was in a coma for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 我被告知我昏迷了六周。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was in a coma for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 是的，我昏迷了六周。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So when did you realize that this was more serious than previous episodes that had sent you to the ER?
sentences.zh: 那么你是什么时候意识到这比之前送你去急诊室的那些发作更严重呢？

sentences.en: I think in the weeks after I woke up, starting to look at all the scars on my body,
sentences.zh: 我想是在我醒来后的几周里，开始看到我身上的所有伤疤，

sentences.en: the nurses would try to get me to do different things in stages.
sentences.zh: 护士们会试着让我分阶段做不同的动作。

sentences.en: And then realizing, like, oh, I can't quite lift up my arm.
sentences.zh: 然后意识到，哦，我抬不起胳膊了。

sentences.en: Oh, I can't quite, like, lift my leg.
sentences.zh: 哦，我抬不起腿了。

sentences.en: Like, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I also could, I couldn't see my legs because they were really wrapped up.
sentences.zh: 我也看不到我的腿，因为它们被紧紧地包裹着。

sentences.en: But I could see my fingers.
sentences.zh: 但我能看到我的手指。

sentences.en: And my fingers had turned black.
sentences.zh: 我的手指已经变黑了。

sentences.en: Like, completely black.
sentences.zh: 就像，完全变黑了。

sentences.en: And so parts of my body died while I was in a coma.
sentences.zh: 所以我在昏迷期间，身体的一些部位坏死了。

sentences.en: And there wasn't enough blood flow to certain parts of my body to continue circulation in a normal way.
sentences.zh: 因为身体某些部位的血液流动不足，无法以正常方式维持循环。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so the decision was made to amputate those parts of my body.
sentences.zh: 所以最终决定截掉那些部位。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, can you explain which parts?
sentences.zh: 为了明确起见，你能解释一下是哪些部位吗？

sentences.en: Well, it was, so it was the fingers on both hands and the legs below the knee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是双手的手指和膝盖以下的腿部。

sentences.en: And so I got amputated nine fingers.
sentences.zh: 所以我截掉了九根手指。

sentences.en: I still have my thumb.
sentences.zh: 我的大拇指还在。

sentences.en: And also both legs below the knee.
sentences.zh: 还有膝盖以下的双腿也都截掉了。

sentences.en: Do you remember what you were thinking and feeling?
sentences.zh: 你还记得当时的想法和感受吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I, um, I would say I was definitely shocked.
sentences.zh: 记得，嗯，我想我当时绝对是震惊的。

sentences.en: But I also sort of, like, took a deep breath and was like, okay.
sentences.zh: 但我同时也深吸了一口气，心想，好吧。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know that I processed it then.
sentences.zh: 我不知道当时自己是否真的消化了这个事实。

sentences.en: I think that I'm processing it now.
sentences.zh: 我想我现在才真正开始消化。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It almost felt like I was in go mode, which it's sort of like a restaurant term where I was like, okay, like, we're going to get through this.
sentences.zh: 我当时几乎进入了“工作模式”，这就像餐厅里的术语，我当时想的是，好吧，我们要挺过去。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 动手吧。

sentences.en: Like the same mentality of being a chef.
sentences.zh: 就像当厨师的那种心态。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like the same mentality of, like, being a cook.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像当厨师的那种心态。

sentences.en: Like, it's like, go mode.
sentences.zh: 就像是，进入工作状态。

sentences.en: Like, let's do this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，开始干吧。

sentences.en: Like, service has been great.
sentences.zh: 就像，服务很棒。

sentences.en: Like, service is going on.
sentences.zh: 就像，服务正在进行中。

sentences.en: It's super busy.
sentences.zh: 非常忙碌。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: Like, we put our heads down.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们埋头苦干。

sentences.en: It felt like it was another step towards my survival.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是为了生存而迈出的又一步。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I wanted to survive.
sentences.zh: 而我想活下去。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Yawande, you were in the hospital for a very long time.
sentences.zh: Yawande，你在医院住了很长一段时间。

sentences.en: You were navigating all of these incredibly difficult things.
sentences.zh: 你一直在应对所有这些极其困难的事情。

sentences.en: I think anybody facing the kind of new reality that you were was probably not immediately thinking of food.
sentences.zh: 我想任何面对你那种新现实的人，可能都不会立刻想到食物。

sentences.en: But in your case, you have written about how returning to food played such a big role in your recovery.
sentences.zh: 但在你的案例中，你写过回归食物对你的康复起到了多大的作用。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit about how it did that.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲它是如何起到作用的吧。

sentences.en: So, I couldn't eat because I was intubated.
sentences.zh: 因为我插了管，所以无法进食。

sentences.en: And then later, when I was feeling a little better, I had a trach inserted into my throat.
sentences.zh: 后来，当我感觉好一点时，我的喉咙里插了气管切开插管。

sentences.en: And I had this, like, ravenous appetite in my head.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里有一种，那种，如饥似渴的食欲。

sentences.en: But I could not experience it in, like, a way where I was, like, experiencing food because I could not eat.
sentences.zh: 但我无法以那种方式去体验它，因为我无法进食。

sentences.en: And that felt, like, even more harmful than anything else.
sentences.zh: 那感觉，甚至比任何其他事情都更让人难受。

sentences.en: Because, like, it almost feels like food is, like, an assurance that I'm alive.
sentences.zh: 因为，食物几乎就像是我还活着的保证。

sentences.en: And then when I got to the point where I could eat, I was only allowed, like, very mildly seasoned things.
sentences.zh: 后来当我能吃东西的时候，我只被允许吃一些调味非常清淡的东西。

sentences.en: And that, again, felt like a type of punishment where it's, like, I only get to eat applesauce.
sentences.zh: 那再次让我感觉像是一种惩罚，就像是，我只能吃苹果泥。

sentences.en: And I can't eat anything with flavor, which is just, like, the worSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我不能吃任何有味道的东西，那简直，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Not what you were craving.
sentences.zh: 不是你渴望的东西。

sentences.en: Not what I was craving at all.
sentences.zh: 根本不是我渴望的东西。

sentences.en: But I did start out slow.
sentences.zh: 但我确实是从慢开始的。

sentences.en: I started out with, like, ice chips.
sentences.zh: 我从，比如，碎冰开始。

sentences.en: Like, can you swallow an ice chip without, like, coffee?
sentences.zh: 就像，你能不加咖啡就吞下一块碎冰吗？

sentences.en: So, it was mostly, like, bread and just jello and applesauce for a while.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一段时间主要是面包、果冻和苹果泥。

sentences.en: What were you craving?
sentences.zh: 你当时渴望什么？

sentences.en: Gosh, I was craving, like, the foods that heal me.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我渴望的是，那些能治愈我的食物。

sentences.en: I was craving, like, foods of my childhood.
sentences.zh: 我渴望的是，童年的食物。

sentences.en: I was craving spicy food.
sentences.zh: 我渴望辛辣的食物。

sentences.en: I remember a friend came in and, like, mentioned something about jello fries.
sentences.zh: 我记得有个朋友来看我，提到了关于“杰洛饭”（Jollof rice）。

sentences.en: And I instantly woke up.
sentences.zh: 我瞬间就清醒了。

sentences.en: I was like, jello fries?
sentences.zh: 我说，杰洛饭？

sentences.en: Can you just describe jello fries for people that don't know?
sentences.zh: 你能为不知道的人描述一下杰洛饭吗？

sentences.en: Just describe it quickly for us.
sentences.zh: 快速为我们描述一下。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Jello fries is, it's essentially a rice cooked in, like, a tomato, onion, and pepper sauce.
sentences.zh: 杰洛饭，本质上是用番茄、洋葱和辣椒酱煮成的米饭。

sentences.en: And it comes out looking, like, bright orange, which is, like, delightful.
sentences.zh: 做出来看起来是亮橙色的，非常诱人。

sentences.en: And it's a very popular dish across West Africa.
sentences.zh: 这是西非非常受欢迎的一道菜。

sentences.en: And then when I got cleared for being able to eat more things, I was well enough to start ordering my own food to the hospital and just, like,
sentences.zh: 后来当我被允许吃更多东西时，我的身体状况已经好到可以开始自己点餐送到医院，并且，

sentences.en: having someone meet the delivery person downstairs and bring me food.
sentences.zh: 让人在楼下接外卖员并把食物带给我。

sentences.en: And I started ordering, like, the most insane things.
sentences.zh: 我开始点一些，最疯狂的东西。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: I started ordering, like, pepper soup from the Nigerian food cart that I knew that was on 42nd Street.
sentences.zh: 我开始点我知道的第42街那家尼日利亚餐车的胡椒汤。

sentences.en: I started ordering carbonara daily almoSt.
sentences.zh: 我几乎每天都点培根蛋酱意面。

sentences.en: And I started ordering a lemon poppy seed muffin with a crumble of lemon poppy seeds on top.
sentences.zh: 我还开始点柠檬罂粟籽松饼，上面还要撒上柠檬罂粟籽碎。

sentences.en: It was the most decadent reintroduction to food.
sentences.zh: 那是对食物最奢华的重新引入。

sentences.en: And I was craving decadence in the way that I had never really done before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未有过这种对奢华的渴望。

sentences.en: Like, I don't wake up and eat tan croissants.
sentences.zh: 比如，我平时不会醒来就吃羊角面包。

sentences.en: But it felt like if someone was coming over and I knew that, oh, you're coming over from the outside world, bring me tan croissants.
sentences.zh: 但感觉就像如果有人要过来，我知道，哦，你从外面的世界过来，给我带点羊角面包吧。

sentences.en: Because all my friends remembered that I loved pastry and I still do love pastry.
sentences.zh: 因为我所有的朋友都记得我喜欢糕点，而且我现在依然喜欢糕点。

sentences.en: And so they would bring different types of pastries for me to try in the hospital, which was, like, such a delight.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会带各种各样的糕点让我去医院尝试，那真是，太令人高兴了。

sentences.en: What did they bring you?
sentences.zh: 他们给你带了什么？

sentences.en: I remember, well, this isn't a pastry, but I remember I would always ask Melissa to bring a salmon bagel.
sentences.zh: 我记得，嗯，虽然这不是糕点，但我记得我总是让 Melissa 带三文鱼贝果。

sentences.en: Is that Melissa Clark?
sentences.zh: 是 Melissa Clark 吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Our food writer.
sentences.zh: 我们的美食作家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She would always bring me a smoked salmon bagel with capers and cream cheese and scallions cream cheese.
sentences.zh: 她总是会给我带一个烟熏三文鱼贝果，配上酸豆、奶油奶酪和葱味奶油奶酪。

sentences.en: And it was wonderful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And because I didn't have mobility in my fingers, she would actually cut it up into, like, little pieces.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我的手指没有活动能力，她实际上会把它切成，小块。

sentences.en: And sometimes it would feed me to just get me to eat because I couldn't do it for myself.
sentences.zh: 有时她会喂我吃，只是为了让我吃下去，因为我自己做不到。

sentences.en: How did it feel to have somebody feeding you?
sentences.zh: 有人喂你吃东西是什么感觉？

sentences.en: I assume that this is the first time that's happened.
sentences.zh: 我想这应该是第一次发生这种事吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, as an adult, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，作为成年人，是的。

sentences.en: I think in those days after I woke up from the coma, I had been poked and prodded and not received a friendly, tender touch in a while.
sentences.zh: 我想在我从昏迷中醒来的那些日子里，我被戳来戳去，已经很久没有感受到友好的、温柔的触碰了。

sentences.en: And so whenever my friends would come visit, I would hold their hands.
sentences.zh: 所以每当朋友们来看我，我都会握住他们的手。

sentences.en: And they would sit with me and, like, beside me or, like, with me in bed.
sentences.zh: 他们会坐在我身边，或者，和我一起躺在床上。

sentences.en: And it felt like I was craving not just foods, but I was craving just, like, a closeness.
sentences.zh: 感觉我不仅渴望食物，我只是渴望，一种亲近感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it felt like an intimate love.
sentences.zh: 那感觉像是一种亲密的爱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When you were finally able to get home, what—can you describe the new reality that you were now faced with?
sentences.zh: 当你终于能回家时，你能描述一下你现在所面临的新现实吗？

sentences.en: And in those early days, what were some of the adaptations you had to make?
sentences.zh: 在最初的那些日子里，你不得不做出哪些适应？

sentences.en: I began to understand what happened to me.
sentences.zh: 我开始理解发生在我身上的事情。

sentences.en: What I could do for myself has completely changed.
sentences.zh: 我能为自己做的事情已经完全改变了。

sentences.en: I can literally open my eyes and sit up in bed.
sentences.zh: 我只能睁开眼睛，在床上坐起来。

sentences.en: And that's the extent of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我能做的全部了。

sentences.en: Mm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Like, this has completely shifted our reality as a family and how I'm able to show up as a member of my family.
sentences.zh: 这彻底改变了我们作为一个家庭的现实，以及我作为家庭成员能够如何参与其中。

sentences.en: Can you give an example or two of what you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你能举一两个例子说明你的意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I think in the mornings, um—so Mark handles everything.
sentences.zh: 我想在早上，嗯——Mark 处理一切。

sentences.en: Mark, your husband.
sentences.zh: Mark，你的丈夫。

sentences.en: He gets the kids up.
sentences.zh: 他叫孩子们起床。

sentences.en: He gets them dressed.
sentences.zh: 他给他们穿衣服。

sentences.en: He makes them breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 他给他们做早餐。

sentences.en: He packs the school lunch.
sentences.zh: 他打包学校午餐。

sentences.en: And I'm able to only observe.
sentences.zh: 而我只能观察。

sentences.en: I can't participate.
sentences.zh: 我无法参与。

sentences.en: How does that feel?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: It feels like grief.
sentences.zh: 感觉像是悲伤。

sentences.en: It feels like I've lost a lot.
sentences.zh: 感觉我失去了很多。

sentences.en: Like, we've lost a lot.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们失去了很多。

sentences.en: That's how it feels.
sentences.zh: 就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: This feels like the reality is hitting, like, the aftermath of it is where the grief is.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是现实正在冲击，就像，后果才是悲伤所在的地方。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Not necessarily, like, the thought about having amputations.
sentences.zh: 不一定是因为，想到截肢这件事。

sentences.en: Not necessarily, like, understanding, like, oh, parts of my body died.
sentences.zh: 不一定是因为，理解了，哦，我身体的一部分坏死了。

sentences.en: But the impact is in the everyday of our life now.
sentences.zh: 而是这种影响存在于我们生活的每一天。

sentences.en: When you're actually experiencing the loss in real time.
sentences.zh: 当你真正实时体验这种损失时。

sentences.en: The loss in real time.
sentences.zh: 实时的损失。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Iwanda, you've been home for some time now.
sentences.zh: 那么，Iwanda，你回家已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's been two years.
sentences.zh: 已经两年了。

sentences.en: And you are now, I understand, learning to use prosthetics.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你现在正在学习使用假肢。

sentences.en: How has that been for you?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说怎么样？

sentences.en: I remember when I first got them.
sentences.zh: 我记得我刚拿到它们的时候。

sentences.en: They felt like props.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉像是道具。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, my God, these are so cool.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，这些太酷了。

sentences.en: But how do I use them?
sentences.zh: 但我该怎么用它们呢？

sentences.en: So, I have upper body and lower body prosthetics.
sentences.zh: 所以，我有上肢和下肢假肢。

sentences.en: And I liken it to watching a baby learn to move their limbs.
sentences.zh: 我把它比作看着婴儿学习活动肢体。

sentences.en: I have to sort of, like, retrain my nervous system to sense that, okay, this is a step that I want to take.
sentences.zh: 我必须，某种程度上，重新训练我的神经系统去感知，好吧，这是我想迈出的一步。

sentences.en: I want to move my leg forward.
sentences.zh: 我想把腿向前移动。

sentences.en: And there's all these, like, muscles and, like, I now have to do, like, stretches, like, 40 minutes every day stretches, like, tummy time.
sentences.zh: 还有所有这些，肌肉，我现在必须做，比如拉伸，每天40分钟的拉伸，比如俯卧时间。

sentences.en: And with my upper limb prosthetics, they're, like, fingers.
sentences.zh: 至于我的上肢假肢，它们就像手指。

sentences.en: And I have to, like, place, put them in a specific way or shape to pick something up.
sentences.zh: 我必须，比如，以特定的方式或形状放置它们来拿起东西。

sentences.en: And you're also back to work now.
sentences.zh: 而且你现在也回去工作了。

sentences.en: I am, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: Okay, so how did you go about doing that?
sentences.zh: 好的，那你具体是怎么做的呢？

sentences.en: Where did you start?
sentences.zh: 你是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: So, I have a caregiver that comes every morning to get me up and get me into a wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 我每天早上都有护理人员来帮我起床，并把我扶到轮椅上。

sentences.en: And I actually started talking to my caregivers, like, where are you from?
sentences.zh: 我其实开始和护理人员聊天，问他们：“你是哪里人？”

sentences.en: What kind of food do you make?
sentences.zh: “你平时做什么菜？”

sentences.en: And they'll be like, oh, I make a goat curry.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：“哦，我会做咖喱山羊肉。”

sentences.en: I'm from Trinidad.
sentences.zh: “我来自特立尼达。”

sentences.en: And I was like, ooh, can we make that together?
sentences.zh: 我就说：“噢，我们可以一起做吗？”

sentences.en: So, I would order all the ingredients.
sentences.zh: 于是，我会把所有食材都订购好。

sentences.en: And we would cook together in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 然后我们在厨房里一起做饭。

sentences.en: And, like, what I would do, it could be as, like, little as, like, whisking something that they hand me in a bowl.
sentences.zh: 我能做的，哪怕只是他们递给我一个碗，我负责搅拌一下，这样的小事都行。

sentences.en: It felt really good to engage in that way and to see that my ability has changed.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式参与其中，并看到自己的能力发生了变化，感觉真的很好。

sentences.en: But, again, like, my love and my passion for food is the same.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我对食物的热爱和激情依然如故。

sentences.en: I understood while I was in the hospital and afterwards that, like, cooking for me is innate.
sentences.zh: 我在住院期间以及出院后都明白了一点：对我来说，烹饪是与生俱来的。

sentences.en: It's something that I'm both compelled to do and also something that I love to do.
sentences.zh: 这既是我不得不做的事，也是我热爱的事。

sentences.en: And I feel like nothing could take that away from me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有什么能把我从这上面剥离。

sentences.en: And it made me think that, okay, I just have to figure out how to do this in my new life.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，好吧，我只需要找出如何在我的新生活中实现这一点。

sentences.en: So, I spoke with my editor, Emily Weinstein.
sentences.zh: 于是，我跟我的编辑艾米丽·温斯坦（Emily Weinstein）谈了谈。

sentences.en: I told her that I figured out a way that I could come back to work.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她，我找到了一种重返工作岗位的方法。

sentences.en: And, of course, she asked me what.
sentences.zh: 当然，她问我是什么方法。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm going to need assistance to help me through the process of, like, submitting a recipe.
sentences.zh: 我说，我需要有人协助我完成提交食谱的过程。

sentences.en: And she said okay to that.
sentences.zh: 她同意了。

sentences.en: One of our producers, Tina Antolini, came to your home to spend a morning with you and your cooking assistant.
sentences.zh: 我们的制片人之一蒂娜·安托利尼（Tina Antolini）来到你家，和你以及你的烹饪助手度过了一个上午。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: As you worked your way through a recipe, just really just sort of observed what that process is now like for you.
sentences.zh: 当你制作食谱时，她只是在观察你现在的操作流程是怎样的。

sentences.en: We are frying mushrooms today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天在炸蘑菇。

sentences.en: When you have a recipe that you want to test with an assistant, how does that process start?
sentences.zh: 当你想要和助手一起测试食谱时，这个过程是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: Okay, so first I come up with an idea, either by something that I've experienced before or something I've imagined.
sentences.zh: 好的，首先我会想出一个点子，要么源于我以前的经历，要么源于我的想象。

sentences.en: And on the day that Tina came, we were working on this interesting concept that I had for a fried mushroom sandwich.
sentences.zh: 蒂娜来的那天，我们正在研究我构思的一个有趣的创意：炸蘑菇三明治。

sentences.en: But I wanted the mushrooms to sort of get the fried chicken treatment where they are crunchy and crisp as a sandwich.
sentences.zh: 我想让蘑菇像炸鸡一样处理，做成酥脆的三明治。

sentences.en: And they sort of shatter when you bite into it.
sentences.zh: 咬下去的时候，它们会发出碎裂的声音。

sentences.en: Delicious.
sentences.zh: 美味。

sentences.en: I think we have a variety of mushrooms, like oyster mushrooms, and then there's, like, really skinny ones.
sentences.zh: 我想我们准备了各种蘑菇，比如平菇，还有那种非常细长的蘑菇。

sentences.en: Next, I write it all down in a recipe format.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我会把所有内容写成食谱格式。

sentences.en: And to do that, I actually just talk to my computer.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我其实只是对着电脑说话。

sentences.en: I send a copy of it off to my assistant.
sentences.zh: 然后我把副本发给我的助手。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Ongi.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是Ongi。

sentences.en: I use these in pronouns.
sentences.zh: 我的代词是they/them。

sentences.en: What background do you bring to doing this work with Yawande?
sentences.zh: 你有什么背景来协助Yawande做这项工作？

sentences.en: I have worked in restaurants since, like, 2018.
sentences.zh: 我从2018年左右就开始在餐厅工作了。

sentences.en: And I do tattoos.
sentences.zh: 我还做纹身。

sentences.en: Ongi did my tattoos.
sentences.zh: Ongi帮我纹过身。

sentences.en: So they make sure I get the ingredients that I need for that specific day.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会确保我买到那天特定需要的食材。

sentences.en: Romaine in the fridge.
sentences.zh: 冰箱里的罗马生菜。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And every day starts at my kitchen table.
sentences.zh: 每天都是从我的餐桌开始的。

sentences.en: The sandwich, the bread's going to be soft.
sentences.zh: 三明治的面包要软的。

sentences.en: That's why I'm not toasting it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我不烤它。

sentences.en: It's just, like, soft.
sentences.zh: 它就是那种软软的。

sentences.en: Where we sit down together, go through the recipe.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在一起，过一遍食谱。

sentences.en: For this recipe, we're going to caramelize the onions firSt.
sentences.zh: 这个食谱，我们要先炒洋葱。

sentences.en: Go through each of the steps.
sentences.zh: 逐一过一遍步骤。

sentences.en: Because I kind of want that, like, onion-y flavor in the oil while we're frying the mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 因为我想在炸蘑菇的时候，油里能有那种洋葱味。

sentences.en: Oh, sick.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Wow, big bread.
sentences.zh: 哇，好大的面包。

sentences.en: Make sure that we each understand what's going on in the recipe.
sentences.zh: 确保我们每个人都理解食谱里的每一个环节。

sentences.en: Then we can fry the mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以炸蘑菇了。

sentences.en: And then we move to the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 接着我们移步到厨房。

sentences.en: So my assistants do the chopping, the slicing.
sentences.zh: 我的助手负责切菜、切片。

sentences.en: You actually don't need it that fine.
sentences.zh: 其实不需要切得那么细。

sentences.en: They see you mincing and, like, you don't need to mince.
sentences.zh: 他们看你切碎，其实你不需要切得那么碎。

sentences.en: Like, roughly chopped.
sentences.zh: 粗切就行。

sentences.en: Roughly chopped.
sentences.zh: 粗切。

sentences.en: They do the blending.
sentences.zh: 他们负责搅拌。

sentences.en: They do the pureeing.
sentences.zh: 他们负责打泥。

sentences.en: They also lift things onto the stovetop, remove things from the stovetop.
sentences.zh: 他们还负责把东西放到炉灶上，或者从炉灶上拿下来。

sentences.en: They lift things from, like, cabinets that I can't reach.
sentences.zh: 他们帮我从我够不到的柜子里拿东西。

sentences.en: I'm going to start frying, heating up the oil.
sentences.zh: 我要开始炸了，把油加热。

sentences.en: They also, like, bring oil up to 10.
sentences.zh: 他们还会把油温加热到10档。

sentences.en: It's almost there.
sentences.zh: 快好了。

sentences.en: They tear apart, like, mushroom pieces.
sentences.zh: 他们负责把蘑菇撕开。

sentences.en: So this is, like, a big clump of mushrooMs.
sentences.zh: 这是一大团蘑菇。

sentences.en: Will you break that up?
sentences.zh: 你能把它掰开吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And then by doing it by hand, you get all of these irregular ridges.
sentences.zh: 用手掰开，你会得到所有这些不规则的纹理。

sentences.en: That tastes so yummy.
sentences.zh: 味道真不错。

sentences.en: They also drop things into, like, a bubbling vat of oil if the process is to fry something.
sentences.zh: 如果流程是油炸，他们还会把东西放进沸腾的油锅里。

sentences.en: It's like walking through each step of the recipe step by step according to how it's written.
sentences.zh: 就像按照食谱上写的，一步一步地走完每一个步骤。

sentences.en: Want to taste it?
sentences.zh: 想尝尝吗？

sentences.en: So while they're working, it tastes good.
sentences.zh: 他们在工作的时候，味道很棒。

sentences.en: I am tasting as they go.
sentences.zh: 我边做边尝。

sentences.en: I like the sharpness and the garlicky flavor.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种鲜味和蒜香味。

sentences.en: I'm, like, taking my wheelchair over to the stovetop to check out what they're doing, how they're stirring, how they're folding.
sentences.zh: 我会把轮椅开到炉灶边，看看他们在做什么，看他们怎么搅拌，怎么翻炒。

sentences.en: I'm listening out for whisking to listen to how a sauce is solidifying with the whisk.
sentences.zh: 我会听搅拌的声音，听酱汁在搅拌下是如何变浓稠的。

sentences.en: I'm sort of like an active observer.
sentences.zh: 我算是一个积极的观察者。

sentences.en: I'm going to say that that's good.
sentences.zh: 我会说，这样就可以了。

sentences.en: That, like, when you shred it and, like, grab a handful and, like, drop it, it should just sort of, like, collapse.
sentences.zh: 当你把它撕碎，抓一把放进去，它应该会塌下去。

sentences.en: Like, in a, like...
sentences.zh: 就像在……

sentences.en: I don't want to say hair.
sentences.zh: 我不想说像头发。

sentences.en: I got it.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: I don't like tinsel.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢金属丝的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, it tastes all tinseled.
sentences.zh: 是啊，吃起来像金属丝一样。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那个。

sentences.en: And so it's about both of us, both me and my assistant, communicating a lot about the recipe, about the cooking process, and about what's going on stove side.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎我们两个人，我和我的助手，我们需要就食谱、烹饪过程以及炉灶边发生的事情进行大量沟通。

sentences.en: And so it's a lot of back and forth and communication.
sentences.zh: 所以会有很多来回的交流。

sentences.en: I would move it to a plate or, like, a board and cut it right through.
sentences.zh: 我会把它移到盘子或案板上，直接切开。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks delicious.
sentences.zh: 我是说，看起来太美味了。

sentences.en: Like, I definitely want to eat that.
sentences.zh: 我绝对想吃那个。

sentences.en: At the very end, we both taste the dish together.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们俩一起品尝这道菜。

sentences.en: We talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论它。

sentences.en: We talk about what works, what doesn't.
sentences.zh: 讨论哪些地方做得好，哪些不好。

sentences.en: Look at that.
sentences.zh: 看那个。

sentences.en: And it's sort of like we go back to the drawing board to see what we made actually follows the format that I imagined.
sentences.zh: 我们就像回到绘图板前，看看我们做出来的东西是否真的符合我预想的格式。

sentences.en: See, that's an obnoxious sandwich.
sentences.zh: 看，那是个夸张的三明治。

sentences.en: That's a whole meal.
sentences.zh: 那是一顿完整的饭。

sentences.en: Do you guys ever disagree?
sentences.zh: 你们会有分歧吗？

sentences.en: I just sort of imagine for somebody like you, maybe it was not super easy to hand over the actual cooking part to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得对于像你这样的人来说，把实际的烹饪部分交给别人可能并不容易。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think working together with someone else in my kitchen, especially in the step where I'm creating a recipe,
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得在我的厨房里和别人一起工作，特别是在我创作食谱的阶段，

sentences.en: the disagreements that we've had have been mostly about, like, whether or not the way it's written will work.
sentences.zh: 我们产生的分歧大多是关于写下来的方法是否行得通。

sentences.en: And what we're doing is trial and error.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是反复试验。

sentences.en: It's like different ways of, like, doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 就像用不同的方法做同一件事。

sentences.en: It sounds like it requires a lot of patience from both of you.
sentences.zh: 听起来这需要你们双方都有很大的耐心。

sentences.en: A lot of patience.
sentences.zh: 很大的耐心。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A lot of patience.
sentences.zh: 很大的耐心。

sentences.en: Yawande's patience, you know, because, like, it's their, like, vision, their dream.
sentences.zh: Yawande的耐心，你知道，因为这是他们的愿景，他们的梦想。

sentences.en: You know, they're, they have an idea of how they want to do it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们对想要怎么做有一个想法。

sentences.en: And then because, you know, we're not the same person, there's so much patience that they have to, like, make sure that's going the way that they want it.
sentences.zh: 然后因为我们不是同一个人，所以他们必须有很大的耐心，确保事情按照他们想要的方式进行。

sentences.en: Yeah, but, you know, it also requires you listening to me.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但你知道，这也需要你听我的。

sentences.en: Like, I don't do this without them, you know, and, like, it's, it's humbling.
sentences.zh: 没有他们我做不到这些，你知道，这让我很谦卑。

sentences.en: And I think patience has, like, this period of my life has, like, taught me so much patience with, like, learning to use my prosthetics.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得耐心……我人生的这段时期，教会了我很多耐心，比如学习使用假肢。

sentences.en: Like, I just have to be patient with myself to be patient with other people.
sentences.zh: 我必须对自己有耐心，才能对别人有耐心。

sentences.en: And that's also allowed you to go back to doing what you love.
sentences.zh: 这也让你能够重新做你热爱的事情。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Like, sometimes I, when I'm in the kitchen with an assistant, I would put on my prosthetics to, like, lip cream just to see if I can do it.
sentences.zh: 有时候，当我和助手在厨房时，我会戴上假肢去打发奶油，只是为了看看我能不能做到。

sentences.en: And those minutes or those, like, times are actually quite thrilling because it feels like me leaning into my former self and actually seeing the cream come together, like,
sentences.zh: 那些时刻其实非常令人激动，因为感觉就像我回到了以前的自己，亲眼看着奶油成型，

sentences.en: the heavy cream come together in, like, a soft whipped cream.
sentences.zh: 浓奶油变成了软软的打发奶油。

sentences.en: And, like, that's like, oh, my God, I did that with a prosthetic hand.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就是，天哪，我用假肢做到了。

sentences.en: Like, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 那太神奇了。

sentences.en: Food is sort of like this continuum between your old self and your present self, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来食物就像是你过去和现在的自己之间的一条连续体。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, I love that, a continuum.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，我喜欢这个词，连续体。

sentences.en: Yeah, because now I'm able to experience food that I had before that I'm having now.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为现在我能够体验我以前吃过、现在也在吃的东西。

sentences.en: Sort of like the immigrant story where, like, I've had a mango in Nigeria and it doesn't taste the same as a mango here.
sentences.zh: 有点像移民的故事，我在尼日利亚吃过芒果，这里的芒果味道就不一样。

sentences.en: But now I'm able to, like, eat a mango and, like, close my eyes and, like, remember, like, oh, my God, like, this is a mango of my childhood, you know?
sentences.zh: 但现在我能吃着芒果，闭上眼睛，回忆起：天哪，这就是我童年的芒果，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And that feels like a through line in my story where, like, food has just really helped me see the through line in my story.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是我故事里的一条主线，食物真的帮我看到了我故事里的主线。

sentences.en: Yawande, thank you so much for all of your time.
sentences.zh: Yawande，非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，Rachel。

sentences.en: This was wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter Show》，我们正准备迎接节假日的客人。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter Show》。
